The final serial conv on the longest path pays off most when a residual shortcut on 0->3 stabilises optimisation of the deep stacked network.

A 3x3 then 1x1 along 0->1->3 forms a cheap spatial-plus-channel pair, whereas without a spatial conv on edge 0 the 1x1 adds little receptive field.
Two identity routes into the output sum are sub-additive and dilute the conv signal, so a second skip helps less when one already exists.
Without 1->3, node 1's features reach the output only indirectly through node 2, so improving edge 0 has a smaller impact.
With 1->2 removed node 1 feeds only one output route, reducing how much a better transformation on 0->1 can propagate.
A deeper serial chain starting at edge 0 trains well across stacked cells when 0->3 provides an identity shortcut alongside it.
